'''Dorado Airport''' or '''Dorado Beach Airport''' {{Airport codes|DDP}}<ref name=GCM /> was a small single runway airport in [[Dorado, Puerto Rico|Dorado]], [[Puerto Rico]].

[[Clara Livingston]], the owner of the property at the time, ordered the strip be built, and her friend, [[Amelia Earhart]], may have used the facility as well.<ref name=Spaced /> Later on, the [[United States]] military, during [[World War II]], paved the runway.<ref name=Freeman />

Much later on, a large airline named [[Caribair (Puerto Rico)|Caribair]] (later overtaken by [[Eastern Air Lines]]), began flights there. When Caribair became part of Eastern, flights to Dorado Airport were suspended.

During the mid 1960s, Dorado was served by [[Dorado Wings]] (later renamed Crown Air), a small airline that operated charter flights between Dorado Airport and [[Luis Muñoz Marín International Airport]] in [[San Juan, Puerto Rico|San Juan]]. The airline operated propeller airplanes.

In the early 1990s, the airport was officially closed. In 1996, the parcel was rezoned and construction commenced of a master planned community: Dorado Beach East. In memory of Dorado Airport and its founder, Ms. Clara Livingston, the developers built a children's playground themed with unique play airplanes, a hangar for activities, and a runway plaza.
